annotations.title: Search Atlas Nodes, Decisions, and Terms

description: Find Atlas entries by topic when you hold no id; an id you already hold can be read directly. Searches Nodes (patterns, concepts, examples) and Roadmap entries (announced, unpublished); kind narrows it to one Node kind, Decisions, or glossary terms. Ids, titles, Hooks (one-line summaries), and claims decide candidacy, Section text only when no subject matches those; order is identity score, then Section score, then how many words matched, then the publisher's order. Returns ranked ids with Hooks (a term's is its whole definition), paged with a cursor. A miss is an empty page; invalid arguments are refused as invalid_argument.

bound.description: How many ranked candidates this call returns; raise it to compare more matches at once, and continue past it with cursor.

cursor.description: scope.next_cursor from a prior atlas_orient page; repeat the same other arguments.

expected_revision.description: Pins this call to the Release (published edition) a prior payload named in 'coherence'; refused as 'revision_changed' if the active Release has changed. Omit for the active Release.

kind.description: Narrows the search to one Node kind, to Decision records, or to glossary terms. Omit it to search every Node kind plus Roadmap entries (announced, unpublished); setting it leaves Roadmap entries out.

examples: keep bulky context out of the window

query.description: A topic or question in ordinary design vocabulary. Words match whole words (four or more characters also match longer words they begin; stopwords drop) in canonical ids, titles, Hooks, and claims, then Section headings and bodies; rarer words weigh more. Section text makes a candidate only when no subject matches elsewhere, so total counts the candidates. kind='decision' searches Decision ids, titles, and bodies; kind='term', keys and definitions. Empty lists every subject of the kind.

name: atlas_orient

data.description: candidates, ranked. A Node candidate has id, hook, and disclosure ('full', or 'roadmap' with its title); a Decision or term candidate has id, which is its atlas_read address, and hook.
